overview: White heads for a King's Indian Attack or colour-reversed Closed Sicilian set-up with d3, Nc3, g3, Bg2 and Nf3. Black can occupy the centre with ...g6, ...d6 and ...e5, or play ...e5 and ...Nf6, so White usually has to be content with a slow, manoeuvring game. It transposes to a Closed Sicilian with colours reversed and rarely offers more than equality.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the bishop and play e4 and f4 for a kingside advance
Keep options of Nf3, O-O and e4, aiming at a reversed Closed Sicilian

black_ideas.idea: Take the centre with ...e5 and ...d5, using the extra tempo
Fianchetto with ...g6 and ...Bg7 and meet White's play on the wings

typical_structures.structure: Closed Sicilian type with colours reversed: White fianchetto, d3/e4 pawns, Black c5/e5 centre

character.notes: Slow, hard to lose, and few forcing lines.

soundness.notes: Sound but passive; Black equalises easily.

structure.notes: The centre stays unresolved with pieces manoeuvring around fixed pawns.

approach.notes: Seldom chosen by strong players apart from surprise use.

sublines_that_differ.name: 1...e5 lines
sublines_that_differ.how: Black takes the centre at once and the game becomes a reversed Philidor.

character.reason: Slow manoeuvring play in which neither king is under early attack.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided and flank pieces manoeuvre.

approach.reason: Strong players mostly use it as a surprise weapon.

level.reason: Plans are clear but need understanding to get an edge.

plans.reason: White fianchettoes and aims for a kingside advance.
